Exercise of Options & Total Voting Rights
TPXimpact Holdings PLC (AIM: TPX), a leading digital transformation partner, announces that it received notification of exercise, in relation to 112,795 share options ("Options") over ordinary shares of 1p each in the Company ("Ordinary Shares") pursuant to the Company's Share Option Plans (the "Exercise").
Accordingly, application has be made for 112,795 new Ordinary Shares to be admitted to trading on AIM (“Admission”). Admission is expected to occur at 8.00 a.m. on or around 23 September 2026.
The new Ordinary Shares will rank
pari passu
with the existing shares of the Company. Following Admission, the Company will have 95,297,304 Ordinary Shares, each with voting rights. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury, therefore the total number of voting rights in the Company is 95,297,304. Accordingly, the figure of 95,297,304 may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in the Company under the FCA’s Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules

latest.title: Contract Wins and Uplifts Totalling £24m
latest.content:
26 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 1322S
TPXimpact Holdings PLC
26 August 2026
26 August 2026
TPXimpact Holdings PLC
("TPXimpact", "TPX" or the "Group" or the "Company")
Contract Wins and Uplifts Totalling £24m
£19m contract uplift and one year extension secured with HM Land Registry and new £5m British Library award
TPXimpact Holdings PLC (AIM: TPX), a leading technology-enabled services company focused on people-powered digital transformation, is pleased to announce two significant contract developments with a combined value of
£24 million
.
HM Land Registry: £19m Contract Uplift
TPXimpact has secured a
£19 million contract uplift
and one year extension under its ongoing strategic delivery partnership with His Majesty's Land Registry (HMLR), extending the contract to May 2028. This extension builds on TPXimpact's appointment in May 2023 as HMLR's primary Digital, Data, and Technology (DDaT) Delivery Partner, originally awarded as a four-year contract to May 2027. The contract was awarded via an open and transparent process using the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework. This extension was included as part of the original contract.
The expanded funding reflects the ongoing growth and success of the joint delivery model, as TPXimpact and HMLR work together to modernise casework systems and accelerate HMLR's transition to a digital-first organisation.
British Library: £5m Contract Win
The Group's digital experience agency,
manifesto
, has recorded its largest ever win, having been selected as the successful bidder to provide digital product development services for the
British Library
as part of its landmark Future Web Programme.
●
Initial Contract Value:
£5 million
●
Contract Duration:
Initial 30-month term, with options to extend
●
Services:
Digital product development, maintenance, and ongoing enhancement of the British Library's web estate via an agile delivery model.
manifesto will supply a multidisciplinary delivery team working alongside British Library staff to modernise the British Library's digital services, expand online access to its collections, and provide a flexible delivery capability tailored to evolving programme needs.
Bjӧrn Conway, Chief Executive Officer of TPXimpact, commented:
"I am delighted with the continued progress being shown by the Group. Securing a further £19m uplift and one year extension with HM Land Registry alongside a major new £5m win with the British Library highlights the exceptional trust our public sector partners place in our delivery teams.
Since we were first appointed as HMLR's core DDaT Delivery Partner in May 2023 under a £49m contract, our joint teams have delivered tangible, modernising changes that directly improve service speed and data quality. Securing this uplift is a testament to the strength of this collaboration and our shared execution track record.
We are equally proud that our digital experience agency manifesto, has been selected by the British Library for its Future Web Programme. Helping one of the world's iconic cultural institutions broaden public access to its vast archives requires adaptable, human-centred digital design-a space where Manifesto excels.
These wins further strengthen our long-term order book and reinforce TPXimpact's position as a key digital transformation partner for the UK public sector."

company_30s.what_they_do: TPX Ltd delivers software and digital services that help public‑sector organisations run their operations more efficiently. Their core products include workflow automation tools, data‑management platforms and integration services that connect legacy systems with modern cloud solutions.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The public‑sector market is large and largely protected by long‑term contracts. TPX’s relationship with the Ministry of Justice and other government bodies gives it a stable revenue stream that can weather market swings. Their technology is positioned to support digital transformation initiatives that many public agencies are prioritising.
company_30s.current_state: TPX appears to be in a period of consolidation after a series of contract wins. The company is still building cash flow, but recent announcements show it has secured sizeable deals (£25m with the MoJ and £24m in other contracts). The share price sits at a very low level, but the company’s valuation remains cheap relative to the contracts it has locked in.

rns_narrative: The company has just announced a new £25m contract with the Ministry of Justice, signalling a significant expansion in its public‑sector portfolio.
Earlier this month it reported a £24m uplift from contract wins, indicating that its sales team is actively closing deals.

Corporate governance updates – a share incentive plan, AGM notice, annual report and major‑holding disclosure – suggest the board is preparing for a period of transparency and potential investor interest.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around a potential upside once the AGM guidance is released.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders are hopeful that the upcoming AGM will reveal stronger guidance and that the MoJ contract will drive a price rally. They see the price as a bargain relative to the contract value.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some market observers worry that the company’s low price and lack of historical performance may keep the stock trapped in a long‑term trough. They fear that the contract wins are not yet generating cash flow and that the company could still be in a cash‑burn phase.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has shifted from neutral to mildly bullish in the last few days, mainly driven by the new MoJ contract announcement. However, overall engagement remains low, suggesting that the broader market is still watching.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for TPX is flat – there is no public search activity, which gives the contrarian a surprise edge if a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM on 5th August is expected to publish updated guidance. A positive outlook could lift sentiment.
Any follow‑up announcements of additional contracts or extensions to the MoJ deal would reinforce the revenue narrative.
A spike in trading volume that breaks the 50‑day moving average could signal the start of a recovery.
If the company releases a quarterly earnings report that shows a clear shift from loss to profit, that would be a strong catalyst.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a breakout above the recent 30‑day support zone, a sudden rise in on‑balance‑volume, and confirmation that the AGM guidance exceeds the current market price.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a deep crash. The APEX score suggests tight compression, so the next move will likely be a sharp bounce if the catalysts materialise.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: TPX has just secured a multi‑million‑pound contract that will generate revenue over several years. The price is very low compared to the contract value, so a mean‑reversion bounce could deliver a 200–300% upside if the stock recovers to the midpoint of its 52‑week range. The contrarian model shows that deep crashes (70‑95% down) often produce the biggest rebounds, and TPX’s recent deal indicates that the market may have already priced in the worst case.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company is still operating at a loss and has not yet demonstrated cash‑flow generation from its contracts. If the AGM guidance remains flat or the MoJ contract is not fully executed, the price could stay below the 30‑day support. A further decline would leave the stock near its 52‑week low, giving a realistic downside of 50–70% from the current level.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is roughly 250% if the price climbs to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, while the maximum loss is capped at the current price because the stock is already near the bottom of its range. The asymmetry is therefore very favourable for a contrarian long.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear breakout above the 30‑day support and a volume spike that exceeds the 50‑day average. Use a position size that allows you to hold 30–50 shares if the price is around 0.10p. Place a stop just below the 20‑day moving average to limit loss to the current price level.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a small position and wait for the AGM. If the guidance is positive and the price moves 5–10% higher on increased volume, consider adding to the position.
playbook.if_passing: If the company announces a regulatory delisting, bankruptcy filing, or a material fraud claim, exit immediately. No other terminal risk is apparent at this time.

ai_insights.bottom_line: TPX is a deep‑crashed, low‑priced public‑sector tech firm that just landed a major MoJ contract; the next catalyst is the AGM guidance – a positive update could trigger a 200% upside while the downside is already capped at the current price.
